cloze.title: Say it the exam way
cloze.text:
Electrons in motion around atomic nuclei each produce a [[magnetic|nuclear]] effect. In iron, nickel and cobalt, magnetic [[dipoles|charges]] can be made to align. The material becomes [[magnetised|charged]]. This is called [[ferromagnetism|gravitation]].

Inside a long solenoid the field lines are straight, parallel and evenly [[spaced|curved]]. An iron core makes the lines more densely [[packed|spread]]. Earth's geographic North Pole is a magnetic [[south|north]] pole.

The strong nuclear force is the strongest of the four forces, but it has the [[shortest|longest]] range. Gravity is the [[weakest|strongest]].

paper2.alt: A solenoid is a helical coil of wire. When there is a current in the wire a magnetic field is produced in and around the solenoid. (c) A ferromagnetic material can be inserted into a solenoid, along its central axis, to increase the magnetic induction. (i) State what is meant by the term ferromagnetic. 1 mark. (ii) Suggest a ferromagnetic material that will increase the magnetic induction. 1 mark. (iii) Predict the effect that the insertion of this ferromagnetic material will have on the magnetic field lines around the solenoid. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2024 Question 14(c). (i) 1 mark: (in a ferromagnetic material) the magnetic dipoles or domains (in the material) can be made to align (resulting in the material becoming magnetised). (ii) 1 mark: iron (or nickel or cobalt). Any other ferromagnetic material is acceptable, such as steel or neodymium. (iii) 1 mark: the field lines will be more densely or tightly packed together, or there will be more of them.

paper2.alt: Two tourists are taking an evening walk while on holiday in the north of Scotland. The aurora borealis or Northern Lights are clearly visible in the night sky. A photograph shows the aurora over standing stones. Tourist 1: It's amazing to think that all that light is because of tiny charges accelerating into the atmosphere. Tourist 2: So where do these tiny charges come from? Tourist 1: Space somewhere? I'm not really sure, but I think it's because they're coming straight down into the magnetic field of the Earth at the North Pole. Tourist 2: Does that explain why we don't see them down south? Using your knowledge of physics, comment on this conversation. 3 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2024 Question 15, open-ended, 3 marks. Award 3 marks for a good understanding of the physics involved, 2 marks for a reasonable understanding, 1 mark for a limited understanding. Candidates may use a variety of physics arguments.

errors: Solenoid: straight, parallel lines inside, and arrows.
Ferromagnetic: dipoles can be made to align.
